title.value: Tackling the Problem of Distributional Shifts: Correcting Misspecified, High-Dimensional Data-Driven Priors for Inverse Problems
title.justification: The title was explicitly found at the beginning of the paper and encompasses the main theme of the study.
title.quote: Tackling the Problem of Distributional Shifts: Correcting Misspecified, High-Dimensional Data-Driven Priors for Inverse Problems

analysis.description: This paper addresses the issue of bias in Bayesian inference due to misspecified priors in high-dimensional inverse problems. The authors propose a method to iteratively update data-driven priors by retraining models with posterior samples, using score-based models as a framework. They demonstrate the effectiveness of their method in improving the alignment of the priors with the true population-level distributions, particularly in the context of strong gravitational lensing.

type.justification: The paper primarily deals with empirical experiments and demonstrations of a proposed method to correct misspecified priors using score-based models in high-dimensional settings.
type.quote: We provide empirical results in high-dimensional settings, showing that this method can forget artifacts present in the initial prior but absent from the true data-generating distribution.

name.justification: The paper applies its methods to the problem of strong gravitational lensing source reconstruction, which requires improving inference of latent parameters from observational data.
name.quote: Here, we showcase our method on the problem of learning idealized brightness structures from noisy and partial observations in the inverse problem setting of strong gravitational lensing source reconstruction.

name.justification: The study involves Bayesian inference techniques to adjust prior distributions based on new observational data.
name.quote: Bayesian inference... provides a mathematical framework for inferring the probability distribution of latent parameters of interest.

name.justification: Score-based models are utilized as the framework for generative modeling in this study, especially for tackling high-dimensional data-driven priors.
name.quote: To demonstrate our method, we use score-based models (SBM), as they have emerged as state-of-the-art generative models for images in recent years.

name.justification: The paper extensively discusses the use of score-based models as a framework to train and adjust data-driven priors iteratively.
name.quote: To demonstrate our method, we use score-based models (SBM), as they have emerged as state-of-the-art generative models for images in recent years.

is_contributed.justification: The paper uses existing score-based models as a framework for its method but does not introduce a new model.
is_contributed.quote: We use score-based models (SBM), as they have emerged as state-of-the-art generative models for images in recent years.

is_executed.justification: The score-based models are trained and retrained iteratively as part of the empirical method proposed.
is_executed.quote: We show empirically in sec. 4 that the procedure does converge to a prior close to the true underlying population distribution for the settings we explored.

is_compared.justification: The paper focuses on the adjustment of priors using score-based models, not on comparing these models numerically against others.
is_compared.quote: We show empirically in sec. 4 that the procedure does converge to a prior close to the true underlying population distribution for the settings we explored.
